# test_reverse_words.py

import pytest

from your_module import reverse_words  # Replace with the actual module name


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("input_string", "expected"),
    [
        ("hello world", "world hello"),
        ("one two three", "three two one"),
        ("Python is fun", "fun is Python"),
        ("hello", "hello"),
        ("hello, world!", "world! hello,"),
    ],
)
def test_reverse_words_happy_path(input_string, expected):
    assert reverse_words(input_string) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("input_string", "expected"),
    [
        ("", ""),
        ("   ", ""),
        ("\t\n  ", ""),
        ("  hello world  ", "world hello"),
        ("hello   world", "world hello"),
        ("hello\tworld\npython", "python world hello"),
        ("  hello\t  world\n python  ", "python world hello"),
    ],
)
def test_reverse_words_whitespace_edge_cases(input_string, expected):
    assert reverse_words(input_string) == expected


def test_reverse_words_preserves_word_characters():
    assert reverse_words("hello-world foo_bar 123") == "123 foo_bar hello-world"


def test_reverse_words_unicode():
    assert reverse_words("こんにちは 世界") == "世界 こんにちは"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "invalid_input",
    [
        None,
        123,
        12.5,
        [],
        {},
        object(),
    ],
)
def test_reverse_words_invalid_non_string_inputs_raise_attribute_error(invalid_input):
    with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
        reverse_words(invalid_input)


def test_reverse_words_bytes_input_raises_type_error():
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        reverse_words(b"hello world")
